dossier.public_summary: The dip alternates between deep and shallow eclipses and shows both a strong secondary eclipse and a very large odd-even difference. Individual transit depths swing from ~170 to ~3000 ppm and sector depths change by half. This pattern matches a blended or on-target eclipsing binary at twice the reported period, not a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by 7 sigma with a 69% depth change, as expected for an eclipsing binary at twice the 14.5 d period (29 d). This is not a stellar-phase artefact.
A secondary dip at phase 0.5546 with SNR 12.38 well above any brightening, at ~36% of primary depth, is a stellar secondary eclipse, unlike a small planet.
Individual transits are not consistent: depth swaps between 172 ppm and ~3069 ppm, the two deep events carry share_of_top_3 0.998 of the signal and drive the odd-even difference.

Depth changes between sectors 16 (1438±180 ppm) and 49 (2383±299 ppm) with a 49% change even within the same SPOC 2-min source, supporting alternating deep/shallow eclipses rather than a stable planet.
